title: Equities: 26 Oct 2026
key_takeaways: S&P 500 rose 0.6% to 5,842; Nasdaq 100 up 0.9% on strong mega-cap earnings, led by Microsoft and Alphabet beats.
ASX 200 gained 0.4% to 8,215, with miners and banks both contributing after the RBA hold was well-telegraphed.
FTSE 100 lagged at -0.2% as sterling strengthened on UK services PMI; European markets broadly flat.

sections.1_equities:

## What moved and why

**US session:** S&P 500 extended gains after Microsoft and Alphabet reported Q3 earnings beats. Microsoft Azure revenue grew 33% year-on-year, above consensus of 29%. Alphabet advertising revenue reaccelerated. Tech (XLK) led sectors up 1.2%; utilities and real estate lagged as 10-year yields held above 4.35%. Small caps (Russell 2000) underperformed the S&P 500 for the fifth consecutive session, reflecting sensitivity to the higher-for-longer rate environment.

**AU session:** ASX 200 opened higher following positive Wall Street lead. Materials (+0.7%) and financials (+0.5%) led. BHP added 0.8% as iron ore held above US$105/t on resilient Chinese steel production data. The four major banks moved in a tight range after the RBA hold confirmed the status quo.

**Other markets:** Hang Seng fell 0.8% as China property developer concerns resurfaced; Nikkei added 0.3% on yen weakness.

## Cross-asset context

US 10-year yields were stable at 4.38%, providing a broadly supportive backdrop for equities - not low enough to drive a rate-sensitive re-rating, but not rising enough to pressure valuations. The USD was marginally weaker (DXY -0.1%), mildly supportive for commodities and EM. The VIX edged down to 17.2, below its 30-day average of 18.5, signalling reduced near-term hedging demand.

## Outlook

Consensus is cautiously constructive into year-end: the soft-landing thesis remains intact, Q3 earnings season has been solid (75% of S&P 500 reporters beating EPS estimates as at 25 Oct), and seasonality is positive. The main risk is a re-acceleration of US inflation that reprices the Fed path. Markets will focus on Friday's US PCE print and next week's FOMC meeting.
